title: The Debate Over Homework
text:
Homework is often defended as a way to reinforce what students learn in class. Supporters argue that repeated practice strengthens memory and gives teachers useful feedback about gaps in understanding. Critics, however, point out that long assignments can leave children tired and reduce the time they spend reading, playing or simply resting. As a result, many schools now limit the amount of homework given to younger pupils.

The debate is complicated by the fact that the value of homework depends heavily on its design. Short, purposeful tasks that build on a lesson are generally considered beneficial, whereas repetitive exercises may do little more than consume evening hours. Parents can help by providing a quiet place to work, although they should avoid doing the work for their children. Ultimately, the goal is to encourage independence rather than dependence.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do supporters believe homework does?
options: It reinforces what students learn in class
It encourages children to read more books
It removes the need for teacher feedback

questions.text: What does paragraph two say about repetitive exercises?
options: They are always the most valuable kind of homework
They are preferred by most parents
They may do little more than consume evening hours
They should be given only to older pupils

questions.text: Why have many schools limited homework for younger pupils?
options: Younger pupils never learn from practice
Long assignments may leave young children with too little time for other activities
Teachers prefer not to give any feedback
Parents have asked for all homework to stop

questions.text: What is the author's implied view of parents who complete their children's homework?
options: They are making the debate simpler
They are working against the goal of independence

vocabulary.definition: to strengthen an idea or skill through repetition or support
information about how well someone is doing, given to help them improve
done with a clear aim or reason
the ability to act or think without depending on others

paragraph_translations: Ev ödevleri genellikle öğrencilerin derste öğrendiklerini pekiştirmenin bir yolu olarak savunulur. Destekçiler, tekrarlı pratiğin hafızayı güçlendirdiğini ve öğretmenlere anlayıştaki eksikler hakkında yararlı geri bildirim sağladığını savunur. Ancak eleştirmenler, uzun ödevlerin çocukları yorabileceğini ve okuma, oyun oynama ya da sadece dinlenme için ayırdıkları zamanı azaltabileceğini belirtir. Sonuç olarak birçok okul artık küçük öğrencilere verilen ev ödevi miktarını sınırlamaktadır.

Ev ödevinin değeri büyük ölçüde tasarımına bağlı olduğu için tartışma daha karmaşık hale gelir. Bir derse dayanan kısa ve amaçlı görevler genellikle yararlı kabul edilirken, tekrarlayan alıştırmalar akşam saatlerini tüketmekten öteye geçmeyebilir. Ebeveynler çocuklarına sessiz bir çalışma alanı sağlayarak yardımcı olabilir, ancak ödevi onların yerine yapmaktan kaçınmalıdır. Nihayetinde amaç, bağımlılığı değil bağımsızlığı teşvik etmektir.
